claim.pdf_says: 11.10.4   General rules  [printed identically to 11.10.1 General, 11.10.2 General format, 11.10.3 Syntax rules - all four are fourth-level subsections of 11.10 PROGRAM-ID paragraph]
claim.markdown_says: ## 11.10.4 General rules   [at '##', while its three siblings are '### 11.10.1 General' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13530), '### 11.10.2 General format' (:13537) and '### 11.10.3 Syntax rules' (:13555)]
claim.why_it_matters: One of four sibling subsections is promoted a level, so the PROGRAM-ID paragraph's General rules detach from the paragraph they belong to and become a peer of '## 11.10 PROGRAM-ID paragraph'. The FORMAT 1 / FORMAT 2 rules for PROGRAM-ID then appear outside 11.10 in any depth-based outline.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds; the underlying observation about the hash count is factually accurate but it is page-break furniture, not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. I rendered page 311 at 300dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v311/spec_p311.png, printed page 281) and read the glyphs myself. The page carries exactly one heading, set bold: '11.10.4 General rules'. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13583 reads '## 11.10.4 General rules', preceded by '' at :13582. Identical clause number, identical title text. Below it the PDF prints 'FORMAT 1', numbered rules 1) through 5), then 'FORMAT 2' and rule 6); the markdown transcribes all eight of those blocks verbatim (:13585-13599), including the cross-references to 8.4.6 Scope of names and 8.6.6 Common, initial, and recursive attributes. No sentence, rule number, format label or heading is absent, altered or reordered. The finding is filed as kind='missing-heading' and nothing is missing -- the kind is a misnomer for what was observed. (2) THE PDF HAS NO ATX LEVEL TO DISAGREE WITH. The only cited difference is the hash count, an artifact of the markdown serialization that has no counterpart in the printed standard. ISO carries clause hierarchy in the clause NUMBER ('11.10.4') plus typographic weight. The number -- the actual hierarchy carrier -- is preserved exactly, and the hierarchical anchor 'section-11-10-4' independently encodes the same nesting. Any consumer needing the outline can derive it from either, unchanged. (3) THE '##' IS MECHANICAL PAGE FURNITURE, NOT A PAGE-311 EVENT. The transcription is chunked per PDF page and resets the heading level at each '## Page N' marker, so whichever clause happens to open a page is emitted at '##'. 11.10.4 opens page 311. I measured this across all 2082 numbered spec headings in the file: 359 headings with 3 or more numeric components are emitted at '##' solely because they open a page. Restricted to 3-component clauses like 11.10.4: page-opening ones are '##' 211 times versus '###' 9 times, while non-page-opening ones are '###' 499 times versus '##' 65. The very heading the claim says 11.10.4 was promoted to be a peer of -- '## 11.10 PROGRAM-ID paragraph' at :13527 -- is itself at '##' for exactly the same reason, because it opens page 310. Page 312 shows the pattern again ('## 12 Environment division' opening the page, then '### 12.1', '### 12.2'), and page 313 shows '## 12.3 Configuration section' promoted above its own siblings 12.1 and 12.2. This is one draw from a pervasive convention, not a defect localized to page 311. (4) THE 'ANY DEPTH-BASED OUTLINE' PREMISE IS FALSE. The file's ATX levels were never a faithful outline, so there was no correct structure for this heading to break. 3-component and 4-component clauses collide on '###': 574 4-component clauses are at '###' (e.g. '### 5.2.6.1 General' :2683, '### 5.2.6.4 Choice indicators' :2698) alongside 499 3-component clauses at '###'. ATX depth therefore already fails to distinguish clause levels in 1073 places. A depth-based outline of this transcription is unusable document-wide, page 311 included and excluded alike; the remedy is one global normalization pass keyed on the clause number, not a page-311 content correction. No COBOL semantics, syntax, or implementable rule is affected. The FORMAT 1 and FORMAT 2 general rules for PROGRAM-ID are present verbatim under a heading numbered 11.10.4, immediately following 11.10.3 Syntax rules, correctly anchored. Per the reconciliation rubric this is formatting plus page-break furniture that does not change meaning: reject.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-311 PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. The heading '11.10.4 General rules' and all six of its FORMAT 1 / FORMAT 2 rules are transcribed verbatim with the correct clause number and a correct 'section-11-10-4' anchor. The sole difference is the ATX hash count, which the PDF does not encode at all. It is produced mechanically by the per-page chunking, which resets the heading level at every '## Page N' marker so that whichever clause opens a page is emitted at '##' -- 359 headings of 3+ numeric components across the file are affected, including '## 11.10 PROGRAM-ID paragraph' itself (:13527, opens page 310) and '## 12.3 Configuration section' (:13639, opens page 313). Separately, the file's ATX levels are not a faithful outline anywhere: 4-component clauses share '###' with 3-component clauses in 1073 places. If this is to be tracked at all it belongs as ONE document-wide cosmetic normalization item -- recompute every numbered heading's ATX level from its clause number, independent of page boundaries -- and not as a structural finding against page 311.
